limits.title: Honest about its limits.
limits.lead: Lighting, dirt and reflections can mislead any comparison.

confidence.title: It states its confidence

retake.title: It asks for a retake

defers.title: It defers to a person

pipeline.title: Seven steps. The model gets one.
pipeline.lead: The cheapest reliable method goes first. Anything that must not be missed is found by plain code, and still works when the model is down.

quality.title: Check the photograph
quality.body: On the phone, as it is taken. A blurred, dark or badly framed shot is rejected at once.

normalize.title: Even it out
normalize.body: Orientation, size and exposure are corrected.

align.title: Line it up
align.body: The return photograph is aligned with its twin from the handover.

regions.title: Find what changed
regions.body: Areas that differ are marked as hints for the next step.

judge.title: Judge
judge.body: The model looks at both photographs and a close crop of each area. It answers no change, wear or damage, and says how sure it is.

price.title: Price
price.body: Each finding is matched to the shop's published list. An amount is never the model's output.

decide.title: Decide

unsure.title: Glare on the brake
unsure.body: The photograph does not allow an answer. A person looks at the item itself.

accuracy.title: Measured, not claimed.
accuracy.lead: The comparison is tested on pairs of photographs whose true answer is known: clean returns, ordinary wear and real damage, in good light and bad.

counts.title: Published as counts
counts.body: Each result is a number of pairs out of the pairs tested, never a bare percentage.

renter.title: The renter's number comes first

worse.title: It cannot quietly get worse

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.lead: Hold is a project built for the PayPal AI Hackathon 2026. It runs in PayPal's sandbox, so no real money moves, and it is not a registered business. This page says plainly what it records, why, for how long, who handles it for Hold, and how to have your details erased.

recorded.title: What Hold records, and why
recorded.lead: Only what a rental needs. No card or bank details: PayPal keeps those.

booking.title: Your booking
booking.body: The name, email and phone number the shop booked you with, your language, the dates and the items. To send you your link, reach you about the rental and show the shop who has what.

payer.title: Your PayPal payment
payer.body: The name, email and account number PayPal gives for the payer, the amounts of the fee, the hold and any charge, and PayPal's own messages about them. PayPal's record is the truth about money, so these are kept as the money log.

photographs.title: Photographs of the item
photographs.body: Taken at handover and at return, and any you send if something happens. They are the evidence of the item’s condition. Faces are blurred in every copy people see; the originals stay locked in storage.

words.title: What you write
words.body: Your answer to a condition report or a claim, your messages to the shop, and what you report during the rental. Kept with the claim or rental they belong to.

phone.title: Texts and the phone app
phone.body: If you choose texts: your number, which texts were sent and whether they arrived. If you use the phone app: an address for its notifications, for that rental only.

record.title: Your Clean Record
record.body: Whether each rental ended clean, under a key that does not name you. Shared with other Hold shops only if you turn that on, and you can delete it yourself from your link.

staff.title: Shop owners and staff
staff.body: Name, email, role and sign-in through Amazon Cognito, and an audit line for everything they do in the shop.

kept.title: How long it is kept
kept.lead: Evidence is kept for a set period, then the storage deletes it itself. Records of money are kept, without the personal details once these are erased.

photographs.title: Photographs and evidence packs
photographs.body: Locked against change or deletion for {lockDays} days, the time PayPal accepts a dispute after a payment, then deleted {keptDays} days after they were taken, with their face-blurred copies.

records.title: Rentals, money and approvals
records.body: Kept while the shop uses Hold, because they are the shop's accounts and cannot be rewritten. The name, email and phone number in them can be erased once the rental has ended.

backups.title: Database backups
backups.body: Kept for {backupDays} days, so an erasure has left the backups {backupDays} days after it.

links.title: Your rental link
links.body: Stops working when it expires, and the shop can withdraw it sooner.

processors.title: Who handles it for Hold
processors.lead: Hold runs on Amazon Web Services in the United States, in the us-east-1 region. These services handle your details only to do the job named here.

aws.title: Amazon Web Services
aws.body: Hosting, the database, photograph storage, queues, staff sign-in through Amazon Cognito, keys and logs. Logs carry no contact details and no photograph contents.

paypal.title: PayPal
paypal.body: Takes the fee, places and releases the hold, and takes any charge a person approved. PayPal handles your payment under its own privacy statement.

claude.title: Anthropic’s Claude, through Amazon Bedrock
claude.body: Compares the handover and return photographs, writes summaries and runs the assistants. It is sent photographs of the item and the least text needed, never your contact details. A request may run in us-east-1, us-east-2 or us-west-2.

rekognition.title: Amazon Rekognition

priceList.wear: Ordinary wear, such as light tyre wear or small scuffs on the pedals, is never charged.

charge.a: No. A hold reserves the amount in the renter's own PayPal account. Nothing is taken unless a person approves a claim.

length.q: How long can a hold stay open?
length.a: Up to 29 days. Hold keeps it valid during the rental and flags any hold that is close to its end before it lapses.

beyond.q: What if the damage costs more than the hold?
beyond.a: The hold is taken in full and the balance is billed separately, with the same photographs attached.

app.q: Does anyone need an app or an account?
app.a: No. Staff open Hold in the browser on the phone they already carry. The renter gets a link.

dark.q: What if a photograph is too dark to judge?
dark.a: Hold asks for it again while the item is still at the counter. If it still cannot tell, it says so and a person looks at the item itself.

wear.q: Who decides what counts as ordinary wear?
wear.a: The shop does, once, in plain words. Hold applies that policy the same way to every renter.

release.a: The moment staff confirm a clean return, usually while you are still at the counter. Your phone tells you that nothing was charged.

chargedFor.q: What can I be charged for?
chargedFor.a: Only damage that is on the published price list, shown in the photographs and approved by a person. A claim can never be higher than the list.

disagree.a: You say so on the same screen and can add your own photographs. A named person at the shop looks at both sides and can lower or drop the charge.

photographs.a: They show the item, not you. Faces are blurred, the photographs are deleted {days} days after they are taken, and the shop can erase your details once your rental has ended.

report.description: A rental shop’s own records from Hold. The money table has one row per movement of money as PayPal recorded it: rental fees and captures to the shop, releases and refunds back to renters, holds placed and renewed. Each money row belongs to a rental; the rentals table says where each rental’s money is now and whether its checks agree. The items table has one row per item with its rentals, days out this year, damage found, damage priced and recovered, and whether it is wearing fastest in its type. Amounts are in the shop’s currency. No renter is named.
